_comment: OPS-MONITORING-INVENTORY-PARITY-W1 (2026-07-28), extended by OPS-AOE-MONITORING-PARITY-W1 (2026-07-29) to a multi-host consumer REGISTRY. SoT for every host-installed monitoring artifact. Reconciled daily by ops/monitoring/monitoring-inventory-reconcile.py (HASH_DRIFT / ORPHAN / DARK / SCHEDULE_DRIFT / PENDING_STALE / REGISTRY_PARITY / NO_BACKUP, plus the DIVERGENT_COPY standing report). A wave that installs, edits, or retires a host monitoring artifact updates its row IN THE SAME COMMIT. Zero-deletion: retired rows are kept, never removed — a retired row is how you prove something was INTENTIONALLY stopped rather than silently lost.

SoT for CLAUDE.md's off-:00 cron law, with exactly TWO consumers and no third derivation: scripts/check-monitoring-schedules.mjs (authoring-time CI gate) and this inventory's own reconciler (the SCHEDULE_DRIFT authority hint). A JS gate cannot import a Python module, so the RULE DATA is the shared artifact and tests/unit/monitoring-schedule-boundary.test.ts pins both implementations to byte-identical verdicts over one fixture corpus. Installed on BOTH hosts because the reconciler runs once per host; a rule file present on only one would make the two hosts render the same drift differently, which is how send_telegram.sh sat behaviourally forked for 7 days.
Self-referential: a file cannot contain its own hash, so sha256 is null and HASH_DRIFT skips it by design (null-sha rows are not compared).

exempt_consumers.detail: These use a zero-dep urllib send path by design, and that is CORRECT rather than tolerated. This wrapper carries ALERT semantics (severity-gated, 24h-deduped, operator-action-required); a per-fire INFO/WARN heartbeat is TELEMETRY, and CLAUDE.md already holds that a by-design fire has no meaningful cooldown threshold. Different contracts, different transports. Do NOT 'fix' these to route through the wrapper.

Declared inbound network posture — the SoT the reconciler's POSTURE_DRIFT check asserts live reachability against. No `schedule`: it is DATA read by the reconciler's own cron, not itself a scheduled job, so DARK does not apply. A SHARED PRIMITIVE under the same canonical + committed-.sha256 + parity contract as send_telegram.sh: both hosts must read the SAME declaration or each would assert a different posture and the peer-vantage comparison would be meaningless. kind=baseline-data so HASH_DRIFT treats a mutation here as SEVERE — an edited posture file silently redefines what 'correct' means, which is worse than a drifted script.

Standing signal for SEC-18. Keyed on RUNNING-vs-newest-INSTALLED kernel, deliberately NOT on /var/run/reboot-required mtime: that file is re-stamped by every new kernel package, so its age is the age of the LATEST trigger and an alert keyed on it resets its own clock monthly (measured at R0 - both hosts read 2026-07-29 while one was 12 and the other 30 revisions behind). Same file on both hosts, ONE canonical sha256 on this row; per-host copies carry no hash of their own. `--self-test` is two-way and vacuity-guarded (>=7 assertions) and proves the send path by capturing the wrapper argv, because both hosts are freshly rebooted and the BREACH branch is unreachable from live state. Fires through send_telegram.sh, which owns severity/cooldown/{NEXT}; smoke it with ALGOVAULT_TG_TEST_INERT=1, never DRY_RUN_TG=1 (that writes the 24h marker and false-greens run 2).

Daily read-only closed-bar divergence report. Runs FROM THE DEPLOY CHECKOUT (ops/cron/** is not in deploy.yml paths-ignore) — deliberately NOT copied into /opt/algovault-monitoring/, which would create a second copy that drifts on every deploy and trips HASH_DRIFT / DIVERGENT_COPY. Alerts only on CANDLE_BASIS_FLIP_READY (once ever, .flip-ready.fired marker) and CANDLE_BASIS_SHADOW_STALLED (n not grown in 48h = a dark shadow write), both via the shared send_telegram.sh. seeded_tfs derived live from crontab -l, never transcribed.

R4: pages ONLY when a HIGH-VOLUME free bucket exhausts the 100/mo cap (burn rate >= QUOTA_CANARY_MIN_CALLS_PER_DAY, default 50/day, i.e. spent the allowance in <=2 days). Ordinary low-volume exhaustion is SILENT BY DESIGN — the alert marks a conversion moment for a caller with no account and no email, not a fault. Dedup identity is (tracker_key, period_start), so a bucket that stays exhausted does not re-fire hourly while the SAME caller exhausting a NEW rolling period does. No sustain gate: a quota counter only climbs within a period, so sustain would add latency and detect nothing. SECRET HYGIENE: a keyed bucket's tracker_key IS the caller's av_free_ API key and is redacted by STRUCTURE (key:sha16:<digest>) in every log line and alert body; keyless free:v2:<hash> ids pass through. Alert body keeps IDs and COUNTS on SEPARATE lines (the 2026-08-01 '(new: 6)' misread class). Prints one QUOTA_EXHAUSTION_CANARY_VERDICT= token per run; the alert contract forces exit 0 on error, so the token is the only thing that can say a run verified NOTHING (INDETERMINATE). --self-test is hermetic (no DB, no wrapper, temp state) and was PROVEN able to fail: four deliberate breaks — bare parenthesised ID, count inside the ID line, removed secret redaction, removed volume threshold, removed period-scoped dedup — each yields SELF-TEST: FAIL. The ID-line assertion is written defensively (no split-index) so a missing label reports FAIL instead of raising. PROBED LIVE BEFORE INSTALL: quota_usage.period_start is a TEXT column (persistTracker writes an ISO-8601 string), so the query casts `period_start::timestamptz` before EXTRACT — without the cast psql errors and the canary would have fail-opened on every single run, i.e. shipped dark. Also verified the algovault_autopilot role can SELECT the table (665 rows). BOOTSTRAP report-not-page on the first cycle: measured 19 exhausted buckets on the host, 5 above the volume threshold, so a naive first run would have paged the whole historical backlog as if it had just happened; the first cycle seeds state silently and only what happens NEXT pages. FIRST LIVE RUN ON THE HOST REPORTED INDETERMINATE, which is the whole reason the verdict token exists: the query was built with %-formatting while its WHERE clause carries SQL LIKE wildcards, so Python raised `unsupported format character` and the fail-open branch swallowed it at exit 0. `build_query` now concatenates. The scenario suite had never touched the SQL path (every case feeds rows through the FORCE_ROWS seam), so four assertions were added that build the query and check the wildcards, the ::timestamptz cast and the limit — each RED-verified by reverting the corresponding piece. The QUOTA_CANARY_FORCE_ROWS seam parses with rsplit(':', 2): a tracker key contains colons of its own (`free:v2:<hash>`), so a left-to-right split reads the count as 'v2' and dies — which is what the first host-side fire-proof hit. Both SQL and seam assertions are wrapped so a raising parser reports FAIL rather than aborting the suite.

Bucket-deterministic dispatch for the TG bot. Lives in the SEPARATE algovault-bot repo (hence the external: artifact ref — this inventory's repo cannot host the ancestor), deployed to /opt/algovault-bot by hand rsync because that tree is NOT a git checkout. On 2026-08-01 a full-tree rsync from a stale Mac checkout DELETED this file, silently reverting dispatch to the relative-age scheduler and restoring the +1min/period ratchet. A HASH_DRIFT/ORPHAN row is the detection that was missing. The durable fix is a git-based bot deploy: OPS-BOT-GIT-DEPLOY-W{NEXT}. Ancestor is committed on algovault-bot main (merged 2026-08-01 by this incident wave), so git IS the recovery path. NO_BACKUP only scans /opt/algovault-monitoring/.

Daily parity between the live /opt/algovault-bot tree and the commit it was deployed from. MISSING is literally the 2026-08-02 failure: a full-tree rsync from a stale shared checkout deleted dispatch_schedule.py and nothing detected it for 90 minutes. Verifies against DEPLOYED_MANIFEST.sha256, written by ops/scripts/host-deploy.sh FROM THE COMMIT — the host has no clone of the bot repo, and hashing the host tree at deploy time would make this check tautological. Reads the deployed path set from ops/deploy/algovault-bot.manifest, the same file the deploy tool reads. Emits one BOT_DEPLOY_PARITY_VERDICT= token; 0=PASS/1=FAIL/3=INDETERMINATE, fails closed. Runs from the deploy checkout like candle-basis-shadow-report.sh, deliberately NOT copied into /opt/algovault-monitoring/ (a second copy drifts and trips DIVERGENT_COPY).

SHA-pinned deploy primitive. Runs on the OPERATOR's machine, not on a host — hence installed_at is empty and host/host_path are n-a rather than invented; it is listed so the registry records the tool that governs deploys, and REGISTRY_PARITY has nothing to assert for it. Refuses any ref that is not an ancestor of origin/main, materializes git archive <sha>, swaps per manifest entry (never whole-directory — /opt/algovault-bot holds a 171M .venv the units execute), sets ownership at the destination including the .bak copy, and stamps DEPLOYED_SHA + DEPLOYED_MANIFEST.sha256. Generic: 7 substantive /opt services share the class it closes; rollout is OPS-HOST-DEPLOY-PROVENANCE-ROLLOUT-W{NEXT}.

Daily provenance assertion for the three GIT-CHECKOUT services on this host (crypto-quant-signal-mcp, algovault-editorial, algovault-blog-assets): HEAD is an ancestor of origin/main, the tree is clean modulo a DECLARED allowlist, and no file is owned by a uid that does not exist. Sibling of bot-deploy-parity.sh but a different evidence source: those services are placed by git, so git IS the lockfile, whereas the bot's tree is placed by ops/scripts/host-deploy.sh and verified against the lockfile that tool writes. Configured by ops/deploy/checkout-parity.conf, which also records the DEFER/EXEMPT set so the un-covered estate is declared rather than forgotten. Emits one CHECKOUT_PARITY_VERDICT= token; 0=PASS/1=FAIL/3=INDETERMINATE, fails closed. KNOWN LIMITATION: `git fetch` fails for algovault-blog-assets (SSH remote, no key for root), so its ancestry is judged against a CACHED origin/main — the run prints an explicit WARNING rather than passing silently. Closing that needs a deploy key: OPS-BLOG-ASSETS-FETCH-KEY-W{NEXT}.

_host_label_semantics: `host` and `installed_at[].host` are OPAQUE STABLE LABELS (`signal-1`, `aoe-1`), never addresses. Label → address resolution happens in ~/.ssh/config or the host's own MONITORING_* env, NEVER from this committed JSON — this repo is PUBLIC. Rows predating OPS-AOE-MONITORING-PARITY-W1 still carry a literal address in `host`; they are NOT retro-scrubbed, because deleting a string from a tracked file does not un-publish it (it persists in git history and in every published image layer). Each reconciler instance declares the labels it owns via MONITORING_HOST_LABELS and evaluates only those rows.
_installed_at_semantics: The CONSUMER REGISTRY — every host+path a shared artifact is installed at. This is the generator-level fix of OPS-AOE-MONITORING-PARITY-W1: the AOE copy of send_telegram.sh was NOT a fork (it was byte-identical to the signal host's own PRE-TEST-CONTEXT-GATE backup, i.e. a pure unmodified ancestor). Two waves updated the primitive at ONE call site because nothing recorded that a second host was also a consumer. Detection alone only tells you the miss already happened; the registry is what makes an update unable to MISS a host. The row's `sha256` is the ONE canonical hash — entries carry no hash of their own (single-derivation: a second recorded hash is a second thing that can drift). `schedule` on an entry overrides the row's for that host.
_exempt_consumers_semantics: Consumers deliberately NOT bound by this artifact's contract, with the ruling that exempted them. Machine-recorded rather than left in an ADR alone: an exemption that lives only in prose gets "fixed" by a future wave enforcing the contract.
